title: feat(objectql,rest)!: refuse a new assignment to a banned user; count and hand over their work
body:
domain:server#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZavYYLh5k5r6jhgCF
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgVoGotjVhGswNmAoy5Ki3yc)_

Part of #30205

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the published `FieldErrorCode` enum gains the member `reference_user_banned`, and a non-system create or update that sets a user field to a user whose ban is in force is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `reference_user_banned`, a write that answered `201` / `200` before. A value the row already stores is not judged.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：新记录不能再指派给已封禁的用户（写入返回 400，字段码 `reference_user_banned`）；新增两条接口，按对象统计某用户名下的记录，并可一次性把它们转给一位在用的用户。
- 为什么改：封禁只会让人下线，他名下的工单、客户还挂着，新的工作也还能派给他，管理员没有办法交接。
- 风险与回滚：这是一次收窄（BREAKING）：以前能成功的「指派给封禁用户」现在被拒。已经存着该用户的记录照常可编辑，系统写入（种子、安装、恢复）不受影响。封禁状态与存在性探测在同一次读取里取回，写入不多花一次查询。回滚就是 revert 本 PR，没有数据迁移。
- 先看：`packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts`（拒绝逻辑）、`packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts` 的 `referenceRow`（探测读取顺带取封禁列）、`packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts`（计数与交接的规则）、`packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.ts`（两条路由）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/engine-banned-user-reference.test.ts`，应看到 10 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的：无。这是非治理路径、低于 3000 行的 BREAKING 收窄，按 pm-dispatch 由席位在合约审查 PASS 后落地；界面一半（封禁对话框显示计数并提供交接）仍在 #30205 上，所以这里写 Part of。

## What changes

**1. A new assignment to a banned user is refused.** The write-time reference check (`assertReferencesResolve`) now also asks, for every caller-supplied value whose target is `sys_user`, whether that user's ban is in force (`banned` is true and `ban_expires` is empty or still ahead), and refuses it with the field code `reference_user_banned` beside `reference_not_found`. The ban columns come back in the existence probe's own read (`referenceRow`, which selects `id` plus the `USER_BAN_FIELDS` the target declares), so a write that names a user pays no read beyond the one it already paid, and the read keeps the probe's elevated, tenant-scoped context: a caller who cannot read the user object is refused the same way. The #29062 rule carries over unchanged: a value every row of the write already stores is not judged, so an edit form that carries the whole record back still saves. A system write keeps its exemption; a flow's `runAs: 'system'` keeps the check, as it does for `reference_not_found`. If the probe's read itself fails, the write is refused for neither reason, as before, and a warning names the field. The check covers every object the engine writes, `sys_*` tables included (a permission-set grant to a banned user is refused too), while the count and hand-over below skip `sys_*` on purpose.

**2. Count a user's work.** `GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/assigned-work` (`client.security.assignedWork.count`) answers, per object and user field, how many records hold the user, counted under the caller's own context. The owner field, `user` fields and lookups to `sys_user` count; platform tables (`sys_*`), `managedBy` objects, disabled packages and `readonly` / `system` fields such as `created_by` do not. Objects the caller cannot read are named in `unreadable`; at most 200 fields are counted (`truncated`). Each count is one query the caller could issue through `/data`; it is an administrator surface, not one to poll.

**3. Hand it over.** `POST /api/v1/security/users/:id/assigned-work/transfer` (`client.security.assignedWork.transfer`) with `{ toUserId, objects? }` moves up to 500 records per call, each as an ordinary `update` under the caller's context, so sharing, validation, approval locks and hooks all apply. It answers per field what moved, what failed (row id, code, and the sentence the `/data` door answers for the same throw, at most 10 per field) and how many remain. A banned, unknown or identical `toUserId` is refused before any write. Multi-valued user fields are counted but not transferred. Neither route touches the ban: the ban stays `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/ban-user`, urgent and alone.

### The new `FieldErrorCode` member

`@objectstack/spec`'s `FieldErrorCode` is a closed response vocabulary, and this PR adds one member, `reference_user_banned`, with its message template in `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` (`validation-message.ts`). That widens the published response face by one member, which is why the declaration is `Clause-②: yes`. It is not an authorable key: no schema an author writes gains, loses or reshapes anything, which is why the changeset carries the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker and `Metadata-protocol: none`. A client that switches on the closed set gains one case; the regenerated `content/docs/references/api/errors.mdx` lists it.

### Where the code lives, and the `engine.ts` touch

- The count and hand-over rules live in `@objectstack/core` (`security/user-assigned-work.ts`): `@objectstack/rest` has objectql only as a dev dependency, so a module both can import at runtime has to sit in core. The ban predicate has one owner, core's `security/user-ban.ts` (#30287): objectql takes `isUserBanInForce` and `USER_BAN_FIELDS` from it through `@objectstack/core`, and `user-assigned-work.ts` through `./user-ban.js`.
- `engine.ts` is in facade form on `main` (#29986), so the read lives in its facet: in `packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts`, `referenceExists` now delegates to a new `referenceRow(target, id, context, extraFields)`, the same `findOne` under `ObjectQL.referenceCheckContext`, which also selects the extra fields the target declares and lets a read error through. The catch stays in `referenceExists`, where the read-seam baseline already records its `null` as the declared third state, and the ban path catches its own call, logs a warning and fails open. `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` gains only a one-line `referenceRow` stub, its slot in the facet host, and the `referenceRow` and `logger` slots in the reference-check host literal; `check:facade-delegation-only` and `check:durability-log-level` are green and the baseline is untouched.

### Census rows the new routes need

- The two routes answer through the shared `sendOk` / `sendError` and are declared to `check:route-envelope` at zero.
- The new REST family `user-work` arrives classified in the authorization conformance matrix: row `anonymous-deny-user-work` (both handlers open with `enforceAuth`), with its booted proof in `showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces.dogfood.test.ts` (anonymous 401 on both routes; a member's count served 200, and a member's hand-over reaching its own unknown-target 404 before any write). The matrix docblock's family figure moves 18 → 19.
- The registrar file joins `REST_SERVER_REGISTRAR_FILES`, the docblock floor (6), the canonical-query table (0) and the `objectQLProvider` consumer census (6 sites). The two routes are `sdk` rows in the route ledger.
- The transfer is a `no-record-echo` row in the internal-fields tripwire and an `ANSWERS_THE_SENTENCE` row in the hook-refusal ledger: a sandboxed hook refusing a moved row reads, in `failures[].message`, as the hook's own sentence, and every fault shape §6 drives keeps its words withheld.
- `user-assigned-work.ts` is classified `not-a-served-read` in core's second-object read-exposure pin: the target read answers only a yes/no about the target, never a row.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-banned-user-reference.test.ts` (10): insert refused and nothing written; the read is elevated (the caller cannot read `sys_user` and is refused all the same); a `user` field and a future expiry; a multi-valued field refused for its banned member only; active and expired-ban users allowed; update refused; a stored value stays editable; a system write is exempt; a missing user stays `reference_not_found`; a user read that throws refuses nothing and logs a warning.
- `packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts` (11): field picking, counts under the caller's context, `unreadable`, disabled packages, the hand-over, per-row failures, the row cap and `remaining`, the three refusals, the elevated target read, and the per-door failure wording. The ban predicate's own tests stay with `user-ban.ts`.
- `packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.test.ts` (7) and `packages/client/src/admin-surfaces.test.ts` (+2).
- The plugin-audit read-cost pins (`audit-milestone-summary`, `audit-option-label-summary`, `implicit-reference-target-summary`) are unchanged and green: a create that names a user still pays zero extra reads.
- The new engine doubles open `update` with `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`, refuse a logical operator rather than read it as a field, and hold a `limit`, so `check:engine-double-contract` (ledger rows recorded with `--write`), `check:where-matcher` and `check:objectql-double-limit` stay green.

## Acceptance notes

- The ui half (the Setup ban dialog showing the counts and offering the hand-over) stays on #30205; this PR does not touch `ui/**`.
- A record already assigned to the banned user stays editable on purpose: refusing it would make every record they held uneditable until someone moved it.
- The transfer does not run elevated. A row the caller could not change by hand is a reported failure, not a skipped one, so `remaining` tells the administrator what is left.
- Any caller who can write a user field can learn that a user id is banned (the probe already disclosed existence); the code is not a secret, and the ui half need not treat it as one.

## Review round 1

Contract review FAIL (comment 6662784185) named five must-fixes; each is in this head:

1. plugin-audit read-count pins red: the ban columns are now read in the existence probe's own `findOne` (`referenceRow`, d5d88743d, moved into the references facet by the main merge ab3fc8d34) instead of a second `find` on `sys_user`. No pin moved; the plugin-audit suite is green at this head.
2. Tracker id in the matrix row's runtime `note:` string: moved to the comment above the row (ed8518156). No baseline entry.
3. Dogfood and gates pinned before the main merge: both re-run in full at this head (Verification below).
4. Declaration: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` here and in the changeset; the BREAKING banner, `patch`, the ADR-0087 marker and `Metadata-protocol: none` stay.
5. `rest-server.ts` docblocks: `registerUserWorkEndpoints` now sits after `registerSecurityExplainEndpoints`, each under its own docblock, and the diff against main in that file is a pure addition (5856fb0fd).

The closing line became `Part of #30205` (no closing verb): the ui half is still open on the card. `main` was merged again (ab3fc8d34) to clear a conflict with the #29986 codemod's fourth pass (#30463) in `engine.ts`; the conflict resolution had moved the probe's catch into `referenceRow`, which the read-seam rule flagged, so a5de9d1e6 puts it back in `referenceExists`.

## Verification

Head `a5de9d1e6` (the landing head), verified locally under the shared verify lock.

- **Dogfood (narrowing arm)**: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` after a full `turbo build`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0, Test Files 420 passed / 3 skipped (423), Tests 3500 passed / 36 skipped (3536), no failures.
- **Suites**: `@objectstack/plugin-audit` 71 files / 1137 tests, including the three read-cost pins; `@objectstack/objectql` 553 files / 11034 tests; lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- **Gates**: all 128 families `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derives for this diff ran, and `--ran` reconciles 128 / 128 at exit 0. One was red on the first run: `@objectstack/spec check:generated`, where `check:test-typecheck`'s `tsc` died without diagnostics under the default heap. Re-run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` it exits 0 with all 14 artifacts current. That is the same heap ceiling earlier rounds hit, not a stale artifact.
- **Targeted**: `check:durability-log-level` (102 read seams, 1 baselined, none stale), `check:facade-delegation-only`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:error-code-casing`, all exit 0.
- **Real boot, before and after** (on `6e44006f9`, before the main merges; the behaviour has not moved since). Run with `pnpm dev -- --fresh`, the showcase app, field `showcase_announcement.owner_id`. "Before" is that head with the ban check and the route registration ablated in `src` and both packages rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight` proved the markers absent from `dist/`, then present again after the restore and rebuild.

  | step | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | create a record owned by B, then ban B | `201` | `201` |
  | **new** record with `owner_id: B` | `201` (assigned to a banned user) | `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `fields[0].code: reference_user_banned` |
  | edit the record that already holds B | `200` | `200` (stored value not judged) |
  | `GET …/users/B/assigned-work` | `404` | `200`, `showcase_announcement.owner_id` count 2 |
  | transfer to a banned user | `404` | `400`, `toUserId` / `reference_user_banned`, nothing written |
  | transfer to the admin | `404` | `200`: `updated 1`, `failed 1` (`RECORD_LOCKED`, the edited record sits in an approval), `remaining 1` |

- **Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, wrap mode, each restored to the HEAD blob):
  - Deleting the ban push turns 4 of the banned-user tests red.
  - Counting with an empty filter turns the count test red.
  - Dropping the banned-target guard turns 2 refusal tests red.
  - Dropping the rest failure describer turns the hand-over row of the hook-refusal ledger red on every §6 shape.
